clips.caption:
Same script, same set, same lighting. It still failed.

Kevin Trudeau tells how a big rival company copied one of his shows down to the host, the set and the interviewer. Side by side, you couldn't tell them apart. Their version still didn't work.

Kevin says the difference was his energy and attitude. They were trying to make money. He was trying to help people with a product he believed in.

Same actions, different intention, different result.

When you do your work, what is your real intention behind it?

hook: Why Dream Before You Have Money
clips.caption:
Your income shouldn't decide how big you let yourself dream.

Kevin Trudeau says most people look at what they earn and then limit what they allow themselves to imagine. In his view, that's not what wealthy people do.

He argues that dreaming big expands your field and your capability, and he quotes the line that a man without a vision will perish.

Dreaming is where the stretching starts, before any plan.

What would you dream about if your current income set no limit?

#ad #money #mindset #success

What if you took life a little less seriously?

Kevin Trudeau asks you to imagine an actor hired to play the villain who kills another character on stage. When the show ends, the two actors go to dinner together. They always knew it was a play.

Kevin says most people forget that life is a play of consciousness. He suggests stepping back, observing your life like a witness, and enjoying the game you're in.

Where in your life have you forgotten that it's a game?

hook: Why Problems Happen For Your Success
clips.caption:
What if hard moments are happening for you, not to you?

Kevin Trudeau shares a phrase he lives by: the universe doesn't do things to us, it does things for us.

He says that after a bad phone call he asked himself why it came in. Maybe the people around him needed to see how someone handles adversity, and that is how they'd handle things going forward.

He doesn't try to list every reason. He asks what the moment could be offering.

What tough moment in your life ended up teaching you something?
